synthesis.body: A rule written in a parent .astro file is scoped to that file: Astro appends the parent's data-astro-cid-* attribute to the selector, and a child component's root element carries the CHILD's cid, not the parent's. So `.child-class { color: X }` written in the parent silently matches nothing — the block compiles, ships, and does nothing. Passing a class through as a prop does not change this. It fails silently, so it can sit in the tree for months (one such block left a copy button wearing the light-zone palette on a dark surface at 3.43:1, under the contrast floor). Fix: have the child expose themable CSS custom properties with fallbacks (`color: var(--x-fg, <default>)`) and set them on an ancestor in the parent — custom properties inherit across the component boundary. `:global()` also works but ties the parent to the child's internal class names and needs a specificity bump to beat the child's own scoped rule.

title: Astro scoped styles cannot restyle a child component from its parent
